changes.headline: Overnight bid on casualty-bearing ship strike and Isaias; Wednesday sold on the IEA release
changes.dek: Brent Dec ~$102.35 (+2.15%), WTI ~$90.1-90.8 overnight; Wednesday WTI -$1.16 to $88.28 on IEA release; Isaias confirmed, Mobile landfall early Oct 10; Qatar tanker strike with casualties. Overnight tape bid: Brent Dec $102.2-102.4 (+~2.1-2.2%), WTI $90.1-90.8 (+~1.3-2.3%) into the Singapore morning (Reuters via Hindu BusinessLine live blog; live benchmarks FT/OilPriceAPI/Convextrade). Brent-WTI back near $12. Two fresh legs: (1) a tanker north of Qatar took multiple projectiles Wednesday with casualties reported (UKMTO via Reuters) - the first casualty-bearing ship hit this round; the Sep 28-Oct 5 window saw 12+ Hormuz-area incidents, the highest weekly rate since the war began; (2) Hurricane Isaias confirmed as the first Atlantic hurricane of 2026 (Reuters, Oct 8) - 75 mph, ~445 mi SSW of the Mississippi River mouth, possible Cat 3 before a Mobile landfall early Oct 10; ~511 kb/d of GoM oil and 16.4% of gas shut in, 8 of 371 platforms evacuated. Wednesday's session: WTI Nov26 settled $88.28 (-$1.16), Brent Dec $100.20 (-$0.38) (Yonhap Infomax) after the IEA agreed to accelerate the strategic release and prioritize diesel. Houthi strikes killed 3 at Saudi airports (1 Riyadh, 2 Abha); coalition hit 80+ Houthi sites late Wednesday; Monday's Mocha claim was premature.
changes.balance_read: The market rents the war premium by the night and returns it by the afternoon: Wednesday's $1.16 WTI loss on the IEA release, then the overnight bid on a casualty-bearing ship strike and a hurricane. The premium leaks on intact flows but the floor stays firm without a diplomatic breakthrough.
changes.publishers: Reuters via Hindu BusinessLine, Oct 8, 2026; Yonhap Infomax, Oct 8, 2026; UKMTO via Reuters, Oct 7-8, 2026

changes.headline: Diesel crack extends $100 regime; IEA now aiming the release at diesel
changes.dek: Diesel crack $105.87 Wednesday close (>$100, third straight); overnight ~$109.27 provisional; IEA now prioritizing diesel in the release. NYMEX diesel crack settled $105.87 on Wednesday Oct 7 - third straight close above $100 (validated against the refreshed crack history; all-time max $117.92, Sep 16 - not a record; first $100+ cross 2022-04-28; 3-2-1 at $67.00 vs $75.31 max Aug 28). The overnight session print runs ~$109.27 (Yahoo front-month bar ~02:00 MDT - provisional, not a close). Diesel futures +3% Wednesday at ~$4.72/gal (zerohedge/Bloomberg). The regime change: the IEA is now prioritizing diesel in the accelerated release, and Trump's Monday executive order waived red-dyed-diesel restrictions - a policy admission that distillate is the binding constraint. EIA's own Winter Fuels Outlook flags East Coast distillates 20-30% below the 5-yr seasonal average. RBN Energy's Oct 7 blog ties record crack spreads to refining economics rather than just war premium. Russia's diesel export ban runs through Oct 31.
changes.balance_read: The release is the ceiling on the product market; the physical drivers (Russia's diesel export ban through Oct 31, hurricane track) are the floor. A Gulf Coast refining track on Isaias tightens the distillate leg further.
changes.publishers: Validated crack history (Yahoo front-month futures), refreshed Oct 8, 2026; Reuters via lapost.com, Oct 7, 2026; RBN Energy, Oct 7, 2026

changes.headline: WCS front holds; December seasonal wide pricing; EIA crude draws on builds expected
changes.dek: TMW Nov26 -$24.62 (-$0.18), Dec26 -$25.15 (+$0.10, still widest); ARV-TMW Nov +$8.93; EIA crude -3.2 Mbbl vs +1.7 expected; Cushing 3rd straight build. ICE settles Oct 7: TMW Nov26 -$24.62 (-$0.18, zero volume - thin front print), Dec26 -$25.15 (+$0.10, still the widest tenor), Jan27 -$23.60, Feb27 -$22.45, Mar27 -$21.75, Apr27 -$20.00. ARV Nov26 -$15.69 (-$0.28), Dec26 -$16.40 (-$0.30). ARV-TMW November spread +$8.93/bbl (implied Hardisty-to-Houston export arb, still healthy). SYN (TMS) Nov26 +$5.87; C5 (TMF) Nov26 +$4.71; MSW (TMR) Nov26 -$1.71; UHC (TMU) Nov26 +$2.40. The ~700 kb/d PADD 2 demand snap-back stands (Joliet restarted ~Sep 28-Oct 2; Whiting at full strength per Reuters Sep 21); Midwest crude processing 'bounced back big time' but remains below year-ago (zerohedge/Bloomberg). EIA (w/e Oct 2): commercial crude drew 3.2 Mbbl vs +1.7 expected; Cushing built a third straight week to 24.75 Mbbl (highest since May); US refinery utilization 92.7%. Gap: the PADD-2-specific utilization % for w/e Oct 2 did not surface in wire coverage - the 85.6% (w/e Sep 25) successor is open. Supply healing: Syncrude coker turnaround Aug 20-Oct 16 per union schedule (completion unconfirmed); CNRL 35-day Horizon upgrader TAR implies ~Oct 12-13; August ST53 data still unpublished. All AESO-monitored SAGD cogen units at full MC (01:39 MDT).
changes.balance_read: September's >$20 WCS blowout (widest since Dec 2023) was a refinery-outage event, not an egress event - and it is unwinding on restarts. The December seasonal wide is pricing; the Nov-Dec egress crunch trades on the ~Oct 19 apportionment notice.
changes.publishers: ICE Report Center EOD, Oct 7, 2026; EIA WPSR w/e Oct 2, released Oct 7, 2026; zerohedge/Bloomberg, Oct 7, 2026

changes.headline: Saudi airport strikes kill 3; coalition retaliates; Hormuz ship hit with casualties
changes.dek: 3 killed at Saudi airports (Riyadh 1+8 wounded, Abha 2+28 wounded); Aden airport ballistic attack; 80+ coalition strikes; Qatar tanker strike with casualties; OPEC+ Nov quotas unchanged. Yemen/Saudi (Oct 7-8): Houthi strikes killed 1 and wounded 8 at Riyadh's King Khalid airport and killed 2 and wounded 28 at Abha airport (Saudi civil aviation authorities via BusinessWorld Online, Oct 8). Houthis fired two ballistic missiles plus drones at Aden airport early Wednesday - one missile landed near the runway minutes before a Cairo flight (Yemen Transport Ministry via Reuters). The Saudi-led coalition struck 80+ Houthi military sites across Saada, Hodeidah, Jawf, and Marib late Wednesday. Monday's Yemeni government claim to have retaken Mocha was premature (military officials via thenews.pk, Oct 8). Hormuz (Oct 7-8): tanker north of Qatar struck by multiple projectiles Wednesday with casualties reported (UKMTO via Reuters) - the first casualty-bearing ship hit this round; 12+ incidents Sep 28-Oct 5, the highest weekly rate since the war began. OPEC+ (Oct 4): November quotas held unchanged at 31.01 Mb/d combined (OilPrice, Oct 5); August actual output ~25 Mb/d, ~5 Mb/d below quota. Next review Nov 1; ministerial Nov 29 sets 2027 policy.
changes.balance_read: Escalation moved from claims to casualties on Saudi soil; barrels still flowing; the bypass is full; diplomacy stalled.
changes.publishers: Reuters/BusinessWorld Online, Oct 7-8, 2026; UKMTO via Reuters, Oct 7-8, 2026; OilPrice, Oct 5, 2026

changes.headline: SPR exchange award pending; Gulf sour pricing awaits
changes.dek: SPR 40 Mbbl exchange award still pending (bids due Oct 7); no DOE announcement. The SPR exchange award is still pending - bids went in Tuesday (11:00 a.m. CT deadline), 40 Mbbl of sour (20 Bryan Mound, 20 Big Hill), Nov-Dec delivery, replacement interest 7.5%/9.5% vs June's 18%. No DOE announcement surfaced as of ~02:05 MDT (confirmed absence) (sixth exchange solicitation under the 172 Mbbl IEA coordinated release; energy-pedia.com, Sep 30). Sparta Commodities (Sep 30) expects Gulf Coast medium grades under pressure through year-end and is watching December Mars FOB below $1/bbl. No fresh Venezuela seizure or Chevron-license news; standing: seven seizures (latest the Sagitta, Sep 29).
changes.balance_read: The exchange award is the next real data point for Gulf sour pricing; the Merey-vs-WCS-vs-Mars triangle at the Gulf is the comp-barrel trade against WCS length.
